subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: What default provider/profile incident policy should OpenClaw use for hard auth failures versus transient 401s, and what redacted status surface should expose it?
rationale: Current main has classifiers and partial skip/status surfaces, but choosing default quarantine timing, transient-auth recovery, and operator-visible health output changes provider routing and status semantics for existing users.

options.title: Default incident-health model
options.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

options.title: Keep opt-in skip only
options.body: Leave default fallback behavior unchanged and improve operator guidance/status, accepting repeated attempts unless operators configure the skip TTL.

options.title: Split restart subcase first
options.body: Repair the config-write restart loop separately before deciding the broader provider quarantine policy.

recommendation.title: Default incident-health model
recommendation.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans auth runtime, provider routing, gateway status, and operator UX, where history shows recent adjacent work.
